title: LED Color and Viewing Angle Explorer

zones.label: Red
zones.summary: The lowest forward voltage of the three, which is why a red LED lights on the smallest supply.
facts: Forward voltage: roughly 1.8–2.2 V, usually quoted as about 2.0 V.
Why it matters: subtract this from your supply before sizing the current-limiting resistor.
On a 5 V supply: about 3.0 V is left across the resistor — the largest headroom of the three colors.

zones.label: Green
zones.summary: A little more forward voltage than red, because shorter-wavelength light takes more energy per photon.
facts: Forward voltage: roughly 2.0–2.4 V, usually quoted as about 2.2 V.
Why it matters: the same resistor gives slightly less current than it would with a red LED.
On a 5 V supply: about 2.8 V is left across the resistor.

zones.label: Blue
zones.summary: The highest forward voltage here — blue light carries the most energy per photon of the three.
facts: Forward voltage: roughly 2.8–3.4 V, usually quoted as about 3.1 V.
Why it matters: a blue LED will not light at all from a supply below its forward voltage.
On a 5 V supply: only about 1.9 V is left across the resistor, so use a smaller resistor than you would for red.

zones.label: Rounded dome
zones.summary: A clear, rounded lens focuses the light into a narrow, bright cone.
facts: How it looks: bright and spot-like from straight on, and it fades quickly as you move off to the side.
Use it for: indicators meant to be read head-on, or anywhere you want reach rather than spread.

zones.label: Flat diffused
zones.summary: A flat, milky lens scatters the light so it leaves over a much wider angle.
facts: How it looks: softer and more even, and still visible from well off to one side.
Use it for: panel indicators seen from odd angles, and anywhere an even glow beats raw brightness.

quiz.question: Which LED color needs the most forward voltage before it will light at all?
quiz.explanation: Blue sits around 3.1 V, so a supply below that will not light it.

quiz.question: Which LED color leaves the most voltage across the resistor on a 5 V supply?
quiz.explanation: Red drops only about 2.0 V, leaving roughly 3.0 V across the resistor.

quiz.question: Which lens shape gives the narrowest, most spot-like beam?
quiz.explanation: A clear rounded dome focuses the light into roughly a 30 degree cone.

quiz.question: You need an indicator that stays visible when viewed from well off to one side. Which lens?
quiz.explanation: A flat diffused lens spreads light over roughly 100 to 140 degrees.

quiz.question: Which color sits between the other two in forward voltage?
quiz.explanation: Green is about 2.2 V, above red and well below blue.
